items.excerpt: Amazon is reportedly building 'Moonraker,' a more powerful agentic version of Alexa+ that can chain multi-step tasks - like booking a ride while texting a friend - across Echo devices. The upgrade is meant to keep Alexa hardware competitive with agentic assistants from Google, Anthropic and OpenAI.

A look at how AI-enhanced smartwatches and health wearables are being trained to flag early signs of illness by fusing heart rate, temperature and other signals against a personal baseline. The piece frames where on-wrist AI health sensing is genuinely useful versus where it overpromises.

RB Labs unveiled 'Robert the Robot,' a humanoid with a digital screen-face, at the UN's AI for Good summit in Geneva - a live gut-check on how far embodied AI still is from natural human interaction. Its awkward expressions underline the gap between humanoid-robot hype and today's real capabilities.

Gizmodo's best-of-June roundup is dominated by AI hardware - Meta's Fury AI glasses running the Muse Spark model, an Insta360 computational vlogging camera, and a Galaxy AI phone with automated app actions. A useful snapshot of which AI devices actually shipped or impressed this month.

Honor's 'Robot Phone' - an AI-hardware play with a 4DoF motorized gimbal camera that pops out and tracks subjects for hands-free mobile filmmaking - is now tipped for an August launch. Built on the Honor-ARRI partnership, it's one of the more radical attempts to fuse AI camera smarts with a moving robotic module in a phone.

Rollme's AirCam is a sub-$80 open-ear bone-conduction headset with an 8MP camera and onboard AI that does real-time object identification and live translation. It's a cheap, oddball stab at the camera-plus-AI wearable category that pricier pendants and smart glasses are chasing.
